 Chicago Fire sidelined its best character, but at least the show had a good reason 
 Chicago Fire's final episode before its two-week break left Severide on the sideline, but the episode thankfully gave us a pair of updates on his status. By Cody Schultz | Nov 19, 2026, 3:52 PM EST Share on Facebook Share on X Share on Reddit Copy Article Add us as a preferred source CHICAGO FIRE — “Mercy” Episode 1404 — Pictured: Taylor Kinney as Kelly Severide — (Photo by: Peter Gordon/NBC) | Peter Gordon/NBC Heading into the final Chicago Fire episode of November, we had a feeling that the show was about to sideline Taylor Kinney . There was no sign of Kinney in any of the promotional materials for the episode, which suggested that Severide would not be featured in the episode. Our instincts were correct, as Chicago Fire season 15, episode 7 ended up sidelining not only Severide, but all of Squad 3. 
--> Heading into the final Chicago Fire episode of November, we had a feeling that the show was about to sideline Taylor Kinney . There was no sign of Kinney in any of the promotional materials for the episode, which suggested that Severide would not be featured in the episode. Our instincts were correct, as Chicago Fire season 15, episode 7 ended up sidelining not only Severide, but all of Squad 3. 
 Unlike in some instances this season when the show has sidelined a major character or group of characters with no acknowledgement of their absence, Chicago Fire did at least provide fans a strong reasoning for why Severide was not in the episode. 
--> Unlike in some instances this season when the show has sidelined a major character or group of characters with no acknowledgement of their absence, Chicago Fire did at least provide fans a strong reasoning for why Severide was not in the episode. 
 As the episode began, quick interaction between Kidd, Violet, and Mouch informed us that Severide was out for the shift, making Kidd the acting head of the house for the episode. 
--> As the episode began, quick interaction between Kidd, Violet, and Mouch informed us that Severide was out for the shift, making Kidd the acting head of the house for the episode. 
 “Wow, look at you—killing it as acting head of house, and it’s not even 9 a.m. yet,” Violet remarked as Kidd turned over a variety of reports to Mouch. 
--> “Wow, look at you—killing it as acting head of house, and it’s not even 9 a.m. yet,” Violet remarked as Kidd turned over a variety of reports to Mouch. 
 "Well, with the probies gone, Severide at NIPSTA with Burke, I kind of didn’t know what to do with myself this morning,” Kidd replied, a reply that was designed to give a quick explanation as to why they wouldn’t be seeing Severide in the episode . 
--> "Well, with the probies gone, Severide at NIPSTA with Burke, I kind of didn’t know what to do with myself this morning,” Kidd replied, a reply that was designed to give a quick explanation as to why they wouldn’t be seeing Severide in the episode . 
 It was a storyline that made perfect sense given how episode 6 ended with Severide offering Burke the open spot on Squad 3 . While Burke had completed his time as a probationary firefighter, being part of Squad requires additional certifications and training. It was expected that Burke would likely miss an episode to take care of these requirements, and it was not surprising when it was revealed that Severide was at NIPSTA (the Northeastern Illinois Public Safety Training Academy) with him, helping him through the various certifications.

It was expected that Burke would likely miss an episode to take care of these requirements, and it was not surprising when it was revealed that Severide was at NIPSTA (the Northeastern Illinois Public Safety Training Academy) with him, helping him through the various certifications. 
 Later in the episode, Kidd offered further information about the duo’s progress when she revealed to Vasquez that Severide had let her know that Burke was cruising through his certifications and they would only miss one more shift. That shift came within the same episode, which means that Severide will be back in action for the show’s final episode of the year before taking a month off.

That shift came within the same episode, which means that Severide will be back in action for the show’s final episode of the year before taking a month off. 
 It was certainly disappointing for Severide to be sidelined in the episode, but we loved that the reason he was not in the episode was because he was personally seeing to Burke and his training. We didn't get to see Severide work closely with Burke when he was a probe at Firehouse 51, and we're excited to see Severide mentor Burke now that he's part of Squad 3.

 After sidelining Severide in episode 7, the promo for the fall finale makes it clear that Severide will be featured front and center. We see Severide and Burke responding to a church fire, and the promo makes it clear that there is something bigger going on than just the fire. Sounds like we might get to see Severide put on his arson investigator cap and give Burke the chance to work alongside him as they look into the cause of the fire and whether there was any foul play, which the promo heavily implies.

 Severide bringing Burke along with him to work on the arson investigation feels like a passing of the baton moment, as it was often Cruz lending Severide a hand on cases. We saw Cruz and Severide team up many times over the years, and we're eager to see what Burke's fresh perspective brings to this pairing and how Severide adapts his mentorship style to help Burke flourish on Squad 3.
